title: Remission is a promised benefit under condition—not an eternal decree already done
source_text: XIII. Quibus in locis, ut apparet, remissio peccatorum proponitur tanquam beneficium quoddam a Deo consequendum, & nobis ab eo promissum, idque sub certa tantum conditione. Unde patet illam minime concipiendam esse, tanquam decretum aliquod, ante tempora secularia factum, a nulla, ex parte hominis, conditione pendens, & per quod peccata, actu & reipsa, homini remissa sint, etiam antequam credat & convertatur. Nec enim decreta Dei sunt promissionum divinarum objecta, & quidem promissionum quae sub conditione fiunt: ut nec pertinent ad eorum numerum, quae, cum ratione, precibus a Deo postulamus; quo de genere non sunt praeterita, sed futura, cum tamen peccatorum nostrorum remissio unum sit ex praecipuis, quae Christus Dominus noster jubet nos a Deo assidue petere, inserta hac, in orationem ab eo dictatam, clausula, Dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut & nos remittimus debitoribus nostris.
pass_a_gloss: In which places, as appears, remission of sins is set forth as a certain benefit to be obtained from God and promised by him to us—and that only under a certain condition. Hence it is clear that it is by no means to be conceived as some decree made before secular ages, depending on no condition on man's part, and by which sins are actually and in reality remitted to a person even before he believes and is converted. For God's decrees are not the objects of divine promises—and especially of promises made under condition; nor do they belong to the number of things which, with reason, we ask of God in prayer; of which kind are not past things but future ones—whereas the remission of our sins is one of the chief things Christ our Lord commands us to ask of God continually, with this clause inserted in the prayer he dictated: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
pass_b_english: Remission is a conditional gospel promise, not a finished eternal decree before faith.
We pray 'forgive us' for what is future to us—not for a past absolute decree.

choices.why: Remission is promised under condition, not bare decree.
